Project guide

Template system

Kite stores metadata in JSON manifests and generated Dart source in readable .tmpl files. This separation keeps templates versionable, testable, and easy to extend.

Template registry

lib/src/templates/registry.json lists every public and internal template:

{
  "id": "feature.mvc",
  "name": "MVC Architecture Feature",
  "type": "feature",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "manifest": "features/mvc/manifest.json"
}

List public templates:

kite templates

Include internal dependency templates:

kite templates --all

Manifest anatomy

{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "id": "component.button",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "requires": ["component.foundation"],
  "dependencies": [],
  "devDependencies": [],
  "files": [
    {
      "template": "files/kite_button.dart.tmpl",
      "target": "{{config.sourceDirectory}}/shared/components/kite_button.dart",
      "upgradePolicy": "replace"
    }
  ]
}

Recursive requirements

requires composes templates without duplicating generation logic:

  1. Load the requested root template.
  2. Resolve its requirements depth-first.
  3. Detect circular dependencies.
  4. Render dependency templates before the root.
  5. Deduplicate identical target paths.
  6. Reject different content targeting the same path.
  7. Merge package dependencies and format once.

Validation

dart format .
dart analyze
dart test
python3 tool/validate_templates.py

The static validator checks registry consistency, manifest IDs and versions, requirements, cycles, source files, conditions, token rendering, safe paths, bundle conflicts, and generated relative imports.
